all_locations: Austin, TX, USA; Salt Lake City, UT, USA
long_description: Launched in February 2021, Jasper is an AI content platform that helps creators and companies of all types expand their creative potential. Over 105,000 active customers are using Jasper to break through writer’s block, repackage their content, create original art, and adjust writing for language and tone. The interest in AI continues to grow and we are at the forefront of teaching the world how to leverage artificial intelligence as a creative partner. We are building teams that will pioneer the content generations space even further.
one_liner: Jasper is a leader in creating content using Artificial Intelligence

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer: Jasper was founded in 2021, but its cofounders go back much further. 8 years ago, Dave Rogenmoser, JP Morgan and Chris Hull sat down and conceived the most wildly ambitious goal they could imagine at that point. 1. Start a company (doesn’t matter what)2. Make $6k/mo to support their families 3. Most importantly, their friendship and commitment to each other would supersede 1 and 2.After shutting down two failed SaaS companies, they finally started a digital marketing agency. Their first client was doing SEO for a porta-potty rental company for $300/mo. After a year, they pivoted and spent the next three years building a course company teaching all things marketing. Courses businesses are great for learning, but hard to scale. They decided they wanted to build a SaaS company and they wanted to go big. That meant we needed to get into YC.

question_answers.question: How did you decide to apply to Y Combinator? What was your experience applying, going through the batch, and fundraising at demo day?
question_answers.answer: The team decided to apply to Y Combinator because they wanted the foundation and acceleration to make a scaleable SaaS company happen.  They initially applied with a company called Proof and were rejected because the idea was too small - more of a feature than a product. After the rejection, they kept building.  They spent six months growing Proof and applied again.  This time they had gone from zero to $175K in 10 months and refined their vision.  The combination of vision plus traction landed them the spot in YC.“YC was amazing,” Dave Rogenmoser later recounted, “I can’t recommend it enough.”  The team worked hard and kept dreaming of where the company was headed. The week after Demo Day they had raised $2.2M at a $12M cap. They moved to Austin, TX, and were on their way.  Over the next two and a half years, the company worked hard on Proof, but in the fall of 2000, growth stalled and that feature-not-a-product challenge persisted.  The founders made the hard decision to pivot and start anew with an AI company.

question_answers.question: What's the history of your company from getting started until the present day? What were the big inflection points?
question_answers.answer: Jasper went from launch to unicorn in 18 months. It’s one of the fastest-growing startups of all time, but like many startups the journey was longer than people may think. The founders first started working together eight years before Jasper’s Series A.  They knew they wanted to build something together but took a few attempts to get to a product with traction.  They started a marketing agency, then a learning platform, then a personalization and social proof company before hitting upon AI.  When they saw generative AI in 2020, they knew how impactful it could be. With marketing roots, they had first-hand experience with the pain that many marketers feel keeping up with content demands and creating enough testing variations to produce good insights.  The idea for Jasper started as a way to create and test ad variations, but they quickly saw how impactful it could be in long-form content and expanded into the AI platform you know today.  Today Jasper is an AI platform built for growing businesses.  When you give Jasper a prompt, it selects from a range of language models the right starting model for your use case, then it can add context about your business, reliable source citations and more current data to improve outputs for your business.  In 2022, Jasper added an extension enabling users to call upon its AI-assistance anywhere they create.  In 2023, Jasper introduced a collection of major new features for business users.   Jasper now has tools for SEO, generating images, checking for plagiarism, collaboration and more.  It is becoming an integral part of how businesses create content that resonates with their target audiences. With its ever-growing suite of features and capabilities, Jasper continues to make content creation easier than ever before for nearly a hundred thousand businesses and growing.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer: For executives and content teams at growing companies, It’s impossible to keep up with content demands. The number of channels, campaigns and topics companies need to cover proliferate every year.  It’s no longer enough to have a blog. You must have a blog, podcast, growing newsletter and social audiences across a half dozen different sites and communities.  Every content creator knows the pain of staring at a blank page on a deadline, and this pressure leads our teams to chase word-count and produce lower quality content.  Jasper helps businesses leverage generative AI to accelerate the writing process so they can give their teams more breathing room for their ideas.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer: Jasper is working to become the AI platform that helps the world’s businesses unlock their best ideas.  We want growing companies to be able to tap AI that matches their brand voice, creates the best possible outcomes for their use cases, and  can be called upon in all the places their teams create.  Along the way we’re working to help businesses transform the way they operate, learn to leverage AI responsibly, and grow.

Moving from messy gate logs and high-risk manual workflows to fast, secure, autonomous access control usually requires breaking legacy systems or throwing more labor at the problem.

Supadock is the multi-agent AI platform for physical logistics operations. We help 3PLs, logistics businesses, and fleets automate facility workflows—starting with the gate. Our agents make sense of visitor credentials, validate documents via bank-grade KYC, identify security gaps, and automate the SOPs needed to secure facility perimeters 24/7, while keeping human oversight for operational exceptions.

Under the hood, Supadock is a multi-modal learning engine. We connect intelligence across your entire facility stack—orchestrating phone calls, emails, text messages, documents, cameras, access control gates, and TMS APIs. The system captures live operational context that compounds into a living model of your business, bringing multi-agent AI into physical logistics operations one SOP at a time.

launches.tagline: We are building autonomy software that tag-teams with human drivers
launches.body:
Hi 👋 [Addwiteey](https://www.linkedin.com/in/addwiteey-chrungoo-06693320/) and [Sandesh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sandeshgwd/) here to introduce [Javelin Robotics](https://www.javelinrobotics.com/).

We help truckers **cut delivery times in half**, doubling productivity and adding much needed capacity to the freight industry. We do this by building autonomy software that tag-teams _with_ human drivers. \
\
Conventional trucks drive \~120K miles/year. Trucks with our tech can hit more than 190K miles/year. Since truckers make money by the mile, this has a direct impact on earnings. Watch [video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hL_vNhlEzOM).

### **Why should you care?**

There is this saying: If its in your home, a truck brought it. Nearly 72% of all freight in America is moved by hard working truckers. 3.5 Million of them. But unfortunately theirs is an ageing pool and not many young folks are joining the workforce. Those who do, frequently quit within a year - a leaky bucket. To add to that, trucks are expected to drive 57% more miles in the coming years to keep up with demand.

### **But aren’t we expecting driverless trucks to solve this?**

To some extent yes, but fully driverless long haul solutions has its own constraints, new costs, new risks and require **major** operational changes to how freight is moved today (i.e. point to point, direct to destination). Driverless freight needs to be routed via hubs → 2x stops, 2x handoffs and offers limited operational flexibility / geographical reach. Most small and medium carriers need operational flexibility + geographical reach.

So if we look at driverless trucks as a tool, its clear they are necessary, but we need complementary solutions that seamlessly work for most.

### **The solution**

Engineer autonomy such that it makes our existing drivers most productive and happy. So, we are building autonomy software that’s designed from the ground up to tag-team _with_ human drivers.

We offer our solution as an end-to-end service: autonomous ready freight search, automated driving in service zones, effortless payments.

![](https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/ohwis2MAaEYhyFZ_A7gxRCUgO6acSak3BzAD5rBNX5T5BDSrnaXTC9vZ9wx9U1AoU0H-rdrt5mfSS5_nxMY0m6f2JWq9UBQApkSzt_TmPPI_1nkfuc6TnjW0JwEa68r6pRSR98LHKrDAu1HHVTRRHrKlhLsj2wArEAh0aZkZfol97pO2knImqZliUBBlPw)

For truck drivers, having access to our software is like having access to a **second driver that drives on-demand.** This helps increase:

* ⏳ **Productivity**
* 🚛 **Trucking capacity**
* 💰 **Driver and fleet revenue**

### **How we are different?**

We’re _not_ building human-less trucks for a few large carriers.

We’re building the **most practical and driver friendly** autonomous system to serve 90% of the trucking industry

* Using existing team driving model truckers are familiar with
* Delivering both operational flexibility and geographical reach
* _No need for_ new infrastructure, process changes or multiple hand-offs
* In sync with current US [federal policy](https://www.whitehouse.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2022/04/04/fact-sheet-the-biden-administrations-unprecedented-actions-to-expand-and-improve-trucking-jobs/) related to trucker jobs
* Similar monetary _savings_ for carriers, as driverless.

Our tech stack’s architecture leverages advances in modern AI, making our dev 10x more capital efficient.

### **About the founders:**

![](https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/X6gKAXbkWpIjj_XRuOC_kTd3henCDJAnZNraOJGg1v6OfearPdJ1rUGqM9gtReiDo9PzeAnXXMvS6bRr-6ArDK_N4PoUazl5BK2N1pPmuPwiBPHSzKwQT9Grx8wyb2CszzCyR-OrlqQNduBd8WtyaToOy2qBNLjMljgMxw3-Mblqivn7RclfFEcCgOj0QA)

[Addwiteey](https://www.linkedin.com/in/addwiteey-chrungoo-06693320/) met [Sandesh](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sandeshgwd/) at Caterpillar where they helped bring the world’s largest autonomous trucks into production. Together, they’ve built autonomous trucks for mines and public highways, from scratch.

For them, It's always been about _robots + people_.

### **How you can help:**

We would love to chat:

* If you or anyone in your network might be interested in learning more or helping out.
* If you are a trucker or run a truck co.
* If you are a shipper looking to ship faster.

**Share this post!**

Please help spread the word. _(many truckers don’t realize autonomy can actually help)._ We can be reached at [founders@javelinrobotics.com](mailto:founders@javelinrobotics.com)

launches.tagline: Multimodal AI employees that see, speak, think and run operations
launches.body:
Hey everyone, we’re [Nuha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/nuhahashem/) and [Alok](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alokhk/) from [Cozmo AI](https://cozmox.ai?utm_source=yc-launch&utm_medium=listing&utm_campaign=launch).

**TL;DR** 

We help banks, insurers and lenders deploy multimodal AI employees that interpret documents and videos, speak with customers in real time, think using your policies and do the work in your core systems.

Check out our [launch video](https://youtu.be/IGypdMioyIo).

**❌ The problem**

If you’ve ever seen how a real customer operation gets handled inside a large company, you’ll notice the conversation is usually the shortest part. Most of the time goes into opening 6-10 tools, finding history, checking documents, verifying details and recording what happened afterwards.

We ran into such issues while building a fintech product and spending months embedded with support and operations teams. A support case that looked “simple” from the outside often meant 40 minutes of prep and follow-up wrapped around an 8-minute customer interaction. The work was more around moving data and decisions across messy systems than actually talking to customers.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98015&key=user_uploads/714894/df0f9156-23c1-46c6-b05f-93060b590053)

To handle these cases, we built an internal system that could understand a case end-to-end and take actions across systems automatically. During a demo, a partner stopped us and asked for that system instead of the fintech product itself.

That became Cozmo.

**✅ How Cozmo is solving it**

Cozmo is a system of work for complex enterprise operations, starting with financial services and insurance. Companies use Cozmo to build and deploy AI employees, which are a collection of agents that own workflows end to end. They talk to customers, read documents, interpret videos, apply company policies and update systems like Guidewire, Temenos and Salesforce, pulling humans into the loop only when real judgment or escalation is needed.

Every decision the AI employee makes is logged, including its reasoning and policy reference, providing a complete audit trail for compliance and operations without additional manual effort. This is managed by our proprietary Agent Protocol Engine (APE), the control layer that keeps shared context, enforces policy and ensures every step is tracked for regulated industries.

Cozmo is live with 10+ enterprises, including Fortune Global 500s like Nestlé, and has already handled over 1M production calls and 10M interactions; cutting costs by up to 70% and turning roughly 1 in 13 conversations into revenue.

[Watch Cozmo in action.](https://youtu.be/ek8eE1bXOnU)

**🧬 What’s unique about Cozmo**

Most AI tools are just prompt trees with a UI. They’re fine for neat, repetitive tasks; but they fall apart the moment operations get messy, ending in half‑filled tickets, off‑script collection calls and disputes scattered across systems.

Cozmo is built for that mess:

* **Multimodal by default:** One platform to spin up AI employees that handle inbound and outbound calls, read PDFs and scanned forms, understand video and talk to customers in a single, continuous flow.
* **Runs on intent, not prompts:** You give it responsibilities and policies like a new hire, instead of maintaining endless prompt chains. As new case patterns appear, the AI employee adapts behavior without you rewriting a graph of scripts.
* **APE-powered coordination:** A single Cozmo “employee” is actually a coordinated team of agents, driven by our Agent Protocol Engine (APE), running an internal loop: planning, delegating, checking and rechecking across systems until the case is closed, not just until a workflow box is ticked.

So instead of a scripted bot, you get something that behaves much closer to a high‑performing operations hire: it keeps context, chases down loose ends and keeps pushing the work forward without you needing to orchestrate every move.

**🚀 Our story**

Nuha and Alok have been friends for over 11 years. We scaled a regulated fintech together in Dubai, navigating one of the most demanding regulatory environments in the world. When the regulations and market changed, we were forced to shut it down. We built AI employees to manage the fintech ourselves on cockroach mode, handling communications and documentation across every affected account. 

That system worked, and when a partner saw it, they asked to buy it instead. So we moved from Dubai to San Francisco to build Cozmo. 

Three years, two countries, 180 pivot, and we’re still going.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=98015&key=user_uploads/714894/4501b459-03fa-4135-9389-d407946bd5ec)

We’re onboarding new enterprise customers in financial services and insurance. If you (or someone you know) run claims, collections or large-scale operations at a bank or insurer, we’d love to connect.

launches.title: ego - an ai-native 3d simulation engine: 👾 getting us closer to the matrix, one pixel at a time
launches.tagline: An AI-native simulation engine and platform where users can create and share 3D animated characters, worlds, games and scripted interactions all using natural language.
launches.body:
**tl;dr**\
_ego is an AI-native simulation engine and platform for AI characters where users can create and share 3D animated characters, worlds, games, and scripted interactions all using natural language. Imagine being able to prompt characters that exhibit human-like behaviour into Minecraft, The Sims, or Animal Crossing into existence._

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79373&key=user_uploads/1552350/b97ac917-413b-465d-af9a-9d43c9091de3)

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bLpG4LrLf60

# Why Now?

The advent of large language models and diffusion models presents an incredible opportunity to solve three seemingly intractable problems in open-world games and simulations:

1. It is hard for humans to write code and script interactions between assets, characters, and the environment to design fun games and experiences
2. It was impossible for NPCs to display human-like behavior and have true agency in these 3D worlds
3. It is hard to create new 3D assets, worlds, and non-playable characters

We founded ego to build an AI native simulation engine to solve all three problems - and we’ve started by tackling the first two. 

[ego](https://ego.live) is an AI-native simulation/game engine and platform where users can create and share 3D animated characters, worlds, and scripted interactions all using natural language. Imagine being able to prompt games like GTA, The Sims, Minecraft, or Animal Crossing into existence.

In the age of Gen AI, it is finally possible to build a **game engine that is also a game**.

# Simulations on ego

Over the course of YC, we built and launched two experimental games with our simulation engine: [TownWorld](https://docsend.com/view/ig6t2shuz26z7wha) (a 3D simulation of the Stanford Generative Agents [paper](https://hai.stanford.edu/news/computational-agents-exhibit-believable-humanlike-behavior) - [tweet thread](https://x.com/peggy_wang/status/1767656498212356597?s=20)) and [CharacterIdol](https://www.characteridol.ai/) (a game where user-prompted generative agents compete to entertain American Idol-style judges…also powered by LLMs). All of the character personalities, conversations, memories, and routines/movements in these games are fully generated by AI.

[Townworld](https://youtu.be/6mPWFFTYebU):

[CharacterIdol](https://youtu.be/j-R1am-kOTY):

This is where we found the massive opportunity to meaningfully make progress toward our vision of gaining usage of our simulation engine - _making it really easy for a user to make and share a game featuring agents in bounded or unbounded 3D space._ We are keenly aware of the sheer amount of time users spend talking to [character.ai](http://character.ai) [characters,](http://character.ai/) as well as the sheer amount of time young creators spend learning Lua code to script simple games and experiences in Roblox. What if we enable humans to interact with agents in immersive 3D worlds without the creators themselves needing to write complex Lua scripts or learn 3D modeling? What if summoning an agent was as simple as filling out a DnD character sheet?

# Why is this a big deal?

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79373&key=user_uploads/1552350/4fffe41d-d395-4029-bc04-15e83365f347)

Since time immemorial, humans have built tools to bring their internal worlds to life. The sandbox, the dollhouse, a tree branch shaped like a rifle - all examples of tools we use to bolster our imaginative capacity to dream new worlds, characters, scenarios, and stories into existence. The closest we’ve come as a species to actualizing our imagination has been through the use of game engines to create simulated open-world experiences and games. AI is about to democratize the strongest tool we’ve had to realize our imaginations, and ego will be the simulation platform and engine that will power this new possibility.

_Animal Crossing_, _The Sims_, _Garry’s Mod_, _Skyrim_, _Minecraft_, _Roblox,_ and _GTA_ - all hit games that empower players to explore, create, and roleplay in immersive 3D worlds. However, video games are hard to build and even harder to keep releasing fresh content for. Outside of the studio system, independent [modders](https://www.nexusmods.com/) have spent countless hours extending these games’ shelf life with new experiences and [characters](https://www.nexusmods.com/skyrimspecialedition/mods/98631), despite heavy technical challenges, and even outright hostility from the original game publishers. 

# Team

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=79373&key=user_uploads/1552350/b74846e9-8f20-4c19-9069-4f070a3838b2)

[Vish](https://linkedin.com/in/astrophysicist) led the FB AI Applied Research team and the Meta Horizon Scripting team. He learned how to program by modding video games as a teenager and also wrote screenplays for films ([Acceptance](https://youtu.be/7r93LEFjpCA?si=fIEMyHdLF5E25aqq)).

* Retweet ([this twitter link](https://x.com/peggy_wang/status/1768405809455825342?s=20)), reshare this ([LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/y-combinator_launch-yc-ego-an-ai-native-3d-simulation-activity-7174147284681564160-taZI))
* Share the launch with friends and gamers who might be interested in trying this out :)
* Try out [characteridol.ai](https://characteridol.ai) and tell us what you think
* Follow [@ego_ai\_](https://twitter.com/ego_ai_) on Twitter
* Optionally follow [@peggy_wang](https://twitter.com/peggy_wang) and [@simulacronist](https://twitter.com/simulacronist) on twitter

   With customizable workflows, deep business logic integration, and advanced automation.

If your company gets more than 5,000 support tickets per month, let us know—we can help. We have a high-touch approach, and our product is super fun to work with (not my words, XD).

launches.tagline: Toma is on a mission to build world-class communication and support tools for America's high ticket industries, starting with automotive.
launches.body:
### **Next-Gen Voice AI in a $2T Industry that Silicon Valley Overlooks**

We’re thrilled to share that Toma [**raised a $17M Series A**](https://techcrunch.com/2025/06/05/tomas-ai-voice-agents-have-taken-off-at-car-dealerships-and-attracted-funding-from-a16z/), led by **Andreessen Horowitz (a16z)**, who chose us after vetting every voice AI company in automotive. The wild part is that we got here through just word-of-mouth sales, without a sales team, and now power **hundreds of customers** across the U.S.

Since graduating from YC, we’ve gone knee-deep into a trillion-dollar industry historically neglected by Silicon Valley––automotive dealerships. We’ve spent half a year **living in them** to learn how they communicate with their customers, run their day-to-day operations, and provide both great and (usually) not-so-great customer experiences. To put it simply, **things are broken**.

So we built AI agents that fix it by:

* Deploying **personalized agents**
* **Automating inbound calls** with a low-latency, natural-sounding voice AI
* Running **outbound SMS** campaigns that generate new revenue
* **Deeply integrating** with automotive-specific software
* Offering **insights and reporting** into every AI/customer interaction
* Intelligently **alerting customers** when human intervention is needed

We’re now the **fastest-growing** AI platform in automotive, and we’re just getting started.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=92511&key=user_uploads/416691/65a56669-51b7-40ff-ad8e-4c443df5a09c)

### **From YC Hack Project to Must-Have AI Employee**

We started Toma as **two engineers** ([Monik](https://www.linkedin.com/in/monikp/) & [Anthony](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anthonykrivonos/)) who didn’t want to build another generic chatbot. We flew around the country, shadowing advisors in hot service bays, listening to call recordings, and mapping dealership workflows in Figma. We **wrote code inside dealerships** as bugs and feature ideas were discovered alongside our users.

We took a YC prototype and turned it into a real product. Today, dealerships such as [Martin Management Group](https://www.toma.com/resources/case-study/how-ai-doubled-operational-margins-for-martin-management-group) and [Middletown Honda](https://www.toma.com/resources/case-study/how-toma-helps-middletown-honda-save-100k-annually) rely on Toma to handle **tens of thousands of calls** monthly. Calls that were previously missing entirely or requiring thousands of dollars to outsource to call centers.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=92511&key=user_uploads/416691/3a60abaf-e5fd-437a-8b4c-f38d911f215e)

### **The Results Are Wild**

* **Martin Management Group:** 9,000 service appointments booked in 90 days. $2M+ in revenue. 40% reduction in BDC workload.
* **Middletown Honda:** 53% of inbound calls handled by AI. $100K+ saved annually. Zero missed calls during recall events.
* **Nationwide:** Over 1 million call minutes handled by Toma since launch. Hundreds of thousands of hours of human time saved.
* **Growth:** Surpassed 7-figures in ARR in less than one year while approaching 8 figures with over 100 dealerships using Toma across the U.S.

The best part is that vehicle owners love it, dealers love it, and Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) love it because **Toma works very well**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=92511&key=user_uploads/416691/85178e79-dde7-4ec7-b19e-b28691d601a4)

### **Why This Industry Matters (and Why It’s Underserved)**

Cars are essential to how Americans live, work, and move, and they’re getting older. The average vehicle on the road is 12.6 years old. That means **more maintenance, more service calls, and more pressure** on dealerships to deliver better experiences.

Silicon Valley has historically **ignored this space**. It’s messy, full of edge cases, and utilizes antiquated software, requiring a deep understanding of real-world operations. **That’s where we thrive.** We see a gold rush in how AI can revolutionize the automotive retail industry.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=92511&key=user_uploads/416691/e94c67ce-14f4-4b8a-8648-3b105052b1d9)

### **Why This Industry is Just the Beginning**

**Automotive** is one of many high-ticket, operationally complex industries in the U.S.—alongside insurance, home services, logistics, and healthcare—where communication is still largely **manual**, software is **legacy**, and workflows are deeply **idiosyncratic**.

These industries are slow-moving but massive, with billions of dollars lost every year due to inefficiencies. While we’re laser-focused on fixing communication in dealerships, Toma is **building the horizontal foundation for deploying production-grade AI assistants** across every high-value, high-friction service industry. We believe the future of operations will be AI-augmented, and we’re laying the rails.

### **The Tech**

**In-house**, we have built:

* A SOTA **voice AI orchestration** pipeline
* **Dynamic integration platform** for connecting to legacy software
* Production-grade **agentic workflow** engine
* **Agent evaluation** pipelines
* **Prompt management** tools that allow us to support hundreds of customers as a 3-person ops team

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=92511&key=user_uploads/416691/2c4115f8-a2bf-433b-b7f3-30f4fa6ca0c3)

### **Our Culture: Builders First, Always**

Toma was **built by engineers**, and we hire technically-minded people across all responsibilities. We move quickly, fix things, and build from the ground up. We care deeply about real-world impact and meticulous attention to detail.

We’re backed by Andreessen Horowitz, Y Combinator, Scale Angels, Flex Capital, Holman Automotive, and more. But more than anything, we’re backed by many of our own dealerships and their staff, who trust us to communicate with their customers.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=92511&key=user_uploads/416691/9eeaaa4c-ba17-4927-82b9-230c362a3684)

### **Who We're Looking For**

You might be a fit if you:

* Want to build **cutting-edge AI features** and work on SOTA everything
* Are **disillusioned by AI slop** products and want to solve real-world problems
* Want **excessive ownership** of critical systems and infrastructure
* Have a **high bar of excellence** and want to work with people who match your energy

If you’re curious, please join us in building the future of AI-powered automotive retail operations. We’re a small team, but we punch above our weight and are having a blast doing it.

👉 [www.toma.com/jobs](http://www.toma.com/jobs)

launches.title: Graphiti by Zep AI : A library for building dynamic Knowledge Graphs
launches.tagline: Accurate, Current Data for AI Agents
launches.body:
Hey! We're Paul, Preston, and Daniel from Zep AI. We've just [open-sourced Graphiti](https://git.new/graphiti), a Python library for building temporal Knowledge Graphs using LLMs.

<https://youtu.be/sygRBjILDn8>

Graphiti helps you create and query graphs that evolve over time. Think of a knowledge graph as a network of interconnected facts, such as _“Kendra loves Adidas shoes.”_ Each fact is a “triplet, represented by two entities, or nodes (_”Kendra,” “Adidas shoes”_), and their relationship, or edge (_”loves”_). Knowledge Graphs have been explored extensively for information retrieval. What makes Graphiti unique is its ability to autonomously build a knowledge graph while handling changing relationships and maintaining historical context.

At Zep, we build a [memory layer for LLM applications](https://www.getzep.com). Developers use Zep to recall relevant user information from past conversations without including the entire chat history in a prompt. Accurate context is crucial for LLM applications. If an AI agent doesn't remember that you've changed jobs or confuses the chronology of events, its responses can be jarring or irrelevant, or worse, inaccurate.

# Zep’s Suboptimal Fact Pipeline

Before Graphiti, our approach to storing and retrieving user “memory” was, in effect, a specialized RAG pipeline. An LLM extracted “facts” from a user’s chat history. Semantic search, reranking, and other techniques then surfaced facts relevant to the current conversation back to a developer for inclusion in their prompt.

Unfortunately, this approach became problematic. Reconciling facts from increasingly complex conversations challenged even frontier LLMs such as gpt-4o. We saw incomplete facts, poor recall, and hallucinations. Our RAG search also failed at times to capture the nuanced relationships between facts, leading to irrelevant or contradictory information being retrieved.

We tried fixing these issues with prompt optimization but saw diminishing returns on effort. We realized that a graph would help model a user’s complex world, potentially addressing these challenges.

# Building Graphiti

We were intrigued by Microsoft’s GraphRAG, which expanded on RAG text chunking with a graph to better model a document corpus. However, it didn't solve our core problem: GraphRAG is designed for static documents and doesn't natively handle temporality.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83738&key=user_uploads/808515/db4712c7-1171-4115-ad7b-67896c754a65)

So, we built Graphiti, a [temporal Knowledge Graph](https://github.com/getzep/graphiti) library, which is designed from the ground up to handle constantly changing information, hybrid semantic and graph search, and scale:

* **Temporal Awareness**: Tracks changes in facts and relationships over time. Graph edges include temporal metadata to record relationship lifecycles.
* **Episodic Processing**: Ingests data as discrete episodes, maintaining data provenance and enabling incremental processing.
* **Hybrid Search**: Semantic and BM25 full-text search, with the ability to rerank results by distance from a central node.
* **Scalable**: Designed for large datasets, parallelizing LLM calls for batch processing while preserving event chronology.
* **Varied Sources**: Ingests both unstructured text and structured data.

# Getting Started

Graphiti is open-source and available on GitHub: <https://git.new/graphiti>

Quick Start: `pip install graphiti-core`

While we developed Graphiti for our needs at Zep, we believe it could be useful for any application dealing with evolving, interconnected data, such as:

* Personal AI assistants that need to maintain user context over time
* Knowledge management systems for rapidly changing domains
* Social network analysis tools
* Financial systems tracking changing relationships and transactions

If you try, we'd love to hear your thoughts, questions, and experiences. Please also consider contributing!

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=83738&key=user_uploads/808515/3d306962-fad2-44fd-9232-862ddd961d0d)

launches.title: Zep: Fast, accurate structured data extraction for AI assistant apps
launches.tagline: 10x faster than GPT-4o, with field format and validity guarantees.
launches.body:
Many business and consumer apps must extract structured data from conversations between an LLM-powered Assistant and a human user. Often, the extracted data is the objective of the conversation. Consider completing a sales order, making a reservation, or requesting leave. All of these tasks require progressively collecting data from the conversation.

Latency and correctness are important. You will often want to identify the correct data values you have collected and those you still need. You’ll then prompt the LLM to request the latter.

<https://youtu.be/k8e8NsoVzFo>

If you’re making multiple calls to an LLM to extract and validate data on every chat turn, you’re likely adding significant latency to your response. This can be a slow and inaccurate exercise, frustrating your users.

Zep’s new Structured Data Extraction feature is a low-latency, high-accuracy tool for extracting the data you need from Chat History stored in Zep's Long-term Memory service.

> **Up to 10x faster than gpt-4o.** For many multi-field extraction tasks, you can **expect latency of under 400ms,** with the addition of fields increasing latency sub-linearly.

## Comparing Zep with LLM JSON Mode

Many model providers offer a JSON inference mode that guarantees the output will be well-formed JSON.

However:

* There are no guarantees that the field values will conform to the JSON Schema you define or that they are correct (vs. being hallucinated).
* All fields are extracted in a single inference call, with additional fields adding linearly or greater to extraction latency.

#### Preprocessing, Guided LLM Output, and Validation

To ensure that the extracted data is in the format you expect and is valid given the current dialog, Zep uses a combination of:

* dialog preprocessing, which, amongst other things, improves accuracy for machine-transcribed dialogs;
* using guided output inference techniques on LLMs running on our own infrastructure;
* and post-inference validation.

You will not receive back data in an incorrect format when using a Zep field type such as email, zip code, or date time.

While there are limits to the extraction accuracy when the conversation is very nuanced or ambiguous, carefully crafting field descriptions can achieve high accuracy in most cases.

#### Up to 10x Faster than OpenAI gpt-4o

When comparing like-to-like JSON Schema model extraction against gpt-4o, Zep is up to 10x faster.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=81733&key=user_uploads/808515/7adc0720-a2ed-43d9-88ed-1bd883f819c7)

Zep's extraction latency scales sub-linearly with the number of fields in your model. That is, you may add additional fields with a low marginal increase in latency.

## Support for Partial and Relative Dates

Zep understands various date and time formats, including relative times such as _“yesterday”_ or _“last week.”_ It can also parse partial dates and times, such as _“at 3pm”_ or _“on the 15th.”_

## Extracting from Speech Transcripts

Zep can understand and extract data from machine-transcribed transcripts. Spelled-out numbers and dates will be parsed as if they were written language. Utterances such as “uh” or “um” are ignored.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=81733&key=user_uploads/808515/8ab99f7f-0672-42dc-9d35-b06c37a33c7a)

## Using Progressive Data Extraction To Guide LLMs

Your application may need to collect several fields to accomplish a task. Since Zep's SDE is so fast, you can guide the LLM through this process by calling the extractor on every chat turn. This enables you to identify which fields are still needed and then direct the LLM to collect the remaining data.

```
You have already collected the following data:
- Company name: Acme Inc.
- Lead name: John Doe
- Lead email: john.doe@acme.com

You still need to collect the following data:
- Lead phone number
- Lead budget
- Product name
- Zip code

Do not ask for all fields at once. Rather, work the fields 
into your conversation with the user and gradually collect the data.
```

## Next Steps

1. Learn more in the [Zep Structured Data Guide](https://help.getzep.com/structured-data-extraction).
2. Sign up for Zep's [Long-term Memory Service for AI Assistants](https://www.getzep.com/).

As interest rates change, demand for mortgages fluctuates dramatically. If hiring is not done early enough, then revenue is left on the table when the mortgage lender cannot service the demand.

At Marr Labs we just announced the launch of Vox Mortgage, an AI voice agent designed specifically for the mortgage industry. Vox enables mortgage lenders to contact borrowers in milliseconds, offering human-like interactions and rapid lead engagement. The AI voice agent’s standout feature is its warm transfer capability, ensuring a smooth handoff from AI to live agents, increasing conversion rates and minimizing call abandonment.

Best of all, Vox Mortgage has unlimited scalability, allowing mortgage lenders to easily scale to make or receive as many calls a day as needed–all with no fixed costs.

This ensures that no leads are lost during transitions, maintaining a natural flow of conversation and maximizing conversion opportunities. Take a listen to a [live Vox Mortgage call](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N9r3f8_jT68). 

### **Accelerating Lead Conversion in Mortgage Lending**

Vox connects with prospective borrowers in milliseconds, allowing lenders to be the first to reach leads after they submit online forms. This first-mover advantage significantly improves lead conversion rates, helping lenders stay ahead of the competition.

### **Seamless Integration and Compliance**

Vox integrates effortlessly with lenders’ existing CRMs, telephony, and loan origination systems. It can also be customized to meet industry compliance requirements, ensuring all communications are secure and meet regulatory standards.

Marr Labs is a pioneer in AI-driven voice solutions, offering human-like, scalable interactions for a variety of industries. **TL;DR**: [Overstand](https://overstandlabs.com/) is a personal data lab for Execs. We allow business leaders validate their intuitions against their company’s data — with their just their voice, you can go from a raw idea to an evidence-backed answer. They can even see a reproducible step-by-step process and underlying data behind it — all in a few in minutes. Have a look at our [launch video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KrOwutgKsEA).\
\
After working with a bunch of larger companies, we learned something important: some of the most valuable questions are not the ones people plan dashboards for. They're the spontaneous ones, the realizations that you have mid-conversation... the "wait a minute…" moments.

Here’s an example that many of us have encountered at some point: let's say you're talking to a customer, and they say "_you know we've really struggled to figure out how to solve X at our company. Is that something you can help us with?_" They might explain why X is hard, and you'd go back and forth a little.

Then you wonder, at some point — is this just them, or have others said the same thing? Has anyone else on your 200-person GTM team heard of _X_ before? The signal is buried across massive email threads, Gong transcripts, Slack threads, and CRM notes — there’s no way to know quickly.

So this intuition fades. Perhaps you’re able to help that customer in a one-off way, but you don’t see the broader pattern.

We built Overstand to solve for this exact gap — the crevices where data collection has traditionally failed to help you. The spurious thought that you might’ve had.

You articulate your intuition in plain language — "_show me all instances of a customer indicating they're struggling with X._" Overstand builds an entire data pipeline on top of your company's comms + hard data and surfaces the underlying examples that answer your questions — in just a few minutes. From there you can drill down: ask follow-ups to hone in on specific instances, chart the results over time or pull everything into a single context to discuss what was found. You can even action each result individually — sending contextually-crafted emails to each customer who mentioned _X_.

All of this, with just your computer or phone (and you can even do it with your voice — we call it _speech-to-data-pipeline_).

Most enterprise tools are built around questions you already know to ask. Overstand is built around the ones you didn't plan for.

If you're running GTM, CS, or product at a company with real customer volume and this problem sounds familiar — we'd love to talk.

launches.tagline: A team messaging platform for humans and agents working together
launches.body:
Hey YC community! What does a normal workflow at a startup look like?

Probably like this:

_> One founder talks to customers_

_> Another founder builds_

_> A customer asks for something. The first founder explains it to the second. The second founder explains it to Claude_

_> Two weeks any one of the founders asks one of the following questions:_

* _Why are we building it this way?_
* _What happened here?_
* _What did we promise ACME we’d do?_
* _How far along are we on X?_

_> Then you scream on the inside because you have to figure out what happened…_

Before agents, the person who did one part of the work usually held a mental map. They could share the context with other people. Increasingly, they can’t.

Small teams can run far more work in parallel than ever before thanks to AI, but someone now has to connect all that context manually. The reasoning behind one product change might now be scattered across a customer call, two emails, a Slack thread, and four Claude conversations.

[Soheil Sadabadi](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/user/727857) and I have been obsessed with solving these problems for a long, long time now.

[Praxos](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/29778) is a team messaging app. 

It has channels, groups and threads like you’d expect. However, places where work happens—Github, harnesses, email, calls—get linked and converted into a living record of your company. This means everyone is always up to date with the latest developments.

Agents can join conversations and inherit the same context humans do.

Here are examples we’ve seen in production:

1. You talk to a customer. Later, when an engineer or coding agent works on the feature, your conversation and the customer’s information are already in context.
2. A new engineer picks up an existing project. They have immediate access to info about who worked on what part of the code base, the deltas across changes, and a granular view of their conversations with coding agents. There’s no need to interrogate the CTO.
3. Three weeks later, someone asks why the engineer made a certain decision about the feature. Praxos fetches the engineer’s convos, the original feature request and call logs between the founder and the engineer. Then it contextualizes the work.

![uploaded image](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/media/?type=post&id=111504&key=user_uploads%2F658480%2F7022badd-c8fc-437c-8e20-0f27d8e6b3d5&variant=large)

We’re early, but the core product already works and is in use. You get messaging, search, memory and connectors. You can bring your own agents, use ours, or both.

A desktop app is going live next week. We’re building native calls and mobile apps, so that all the communications that go into a company’s history can happen on Praxos.

**Our ask:** if you’re a 2 to 10 person team where one person is spending all day with customers while the rest of the team is shipping with Claude/Codex, we’d love to personally onboard you.

Especially if you’ve already caught yourself asking “what did the customer want?” or “what’s going on with X?” last week.

The first 10 teams get

[Praxos](https://bookface.ycombinator.com/company/29778) for free for 6 months ;)

Email me at [lucas@praxos.ai](mailto:lucas@praxos.ai).

If you’re building voice AI agents and want a faster, smarter way to test and improve them, we’d love to connect! Email [james@roark.ai](mailto:james@roark.ai) or [book a time here](https://calendly.com/james-roark/book-a-demo).

## **The Problem: Testing Voice AI Is Painfully Manual**

Once a voice agent is live, teams have no easy way to test updates. Every time you tweak a prompt or logic, you have to manually call the bot, hoping to catch issues before customers do.

* Does the agent follow the right flow? You don’t know unless you re-run conversations by hand.
* Did a change break something? You won’t find out until users complain.
* How do customers actually experience the bot? Traditional testing tools only analyze text transcripts, missing tone, hesitation, or frustration.

Voice AI teams, especially in healthcare, legal, and customer support need real-world validation for every change they ship. But existing testing tools rely on scripted test cases that don’t reflect real interactions, leading to blind spots and regressions.

## **The Solution**

Roark lets you replay real production calls against your newest AI logic, so you can test changes before they go live. No more manually dialing your bot or relying on outdated scripted tests - get real-world validation instantly.

How It Works:

1. Capture real-world calls: Automatically ingest production conversations from your existing voice AI setup (integrates seamlessly with VAPI, Retell, or custom APIs).
2. Replay calls on your updated agent: Our system re-runs the same user inputs, sentiment, and tone against your latest agent, cloning the original caller’s voice for more realistic testing.
3. Evaluate goal completion: Define key objectives (e.g., “Did the agent confirm insurance?”) and automatically flag failures or missteps.
4. Monitor sentiment & vocal cues: Detect frustration, long pauses, sighs, and hesitation - signals that text-based evaluations miss.
5. Track performance with reports & dashboards: Visualize conversation flows, track drop-offs, and measure key metrics with Mixpanel-style analytics.
6. Get real-time alerts: Set up custom monitoring for compliance violations, negative sentiment spikes, or repeated failures.

Roark gives AI teams the same confidence in testing, iteration, and monitoring that software engineers had for years with modern dev tools.

Check out our demo below!

<https://youtu.be/eu8mo28LsTc?feature=shared>

## **Why We Built Roark**

We first ran into this problem while building a voice agent for a dental clinic. Patients kept reporting issues, getting stuck in loops, failing to confirm insurance, or receiving irrelevant responses. But the only way to test fixes was to call the bot ourselves or read through hundreds of transcripts, hoping to spot patterns. It was frustrating, slow, and unreliable.

After talking to other teams working on Voice AI, we realized this problem was universal - everyone was struggling to validate their AI’s performance efficiently. That’s when we decided to build Roark.

launches.body:
We have trained an AI model called Orator, that speaks Urdu with human-like realism. To the best of our knowledge, it is the first model that can speak Urdu in an authentic way: the way everyday people speak Urdu in everyday life.

We have voices from “the whole mohalla“ (entire neighborhood). From angry molvis and nosey aunties, to thailay walas, and burger boys.

**You can experience the voices at [UpliftAI.org](http://UpliftAI.org).** The website will allow you to experience dozens of voices in seconds by just clicking/hovering the circles.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103672&key=user_uploads/1455159/ac1e7d0f-ca3e-4fc0-aac6-4cc61a89797e)

**Making the model**

We have put our heart into this work, and enjoying it more than any work we have ever done in the past.

We started with the map of Pakistan and asked: how do people sound in every district. That gave us the accent list.

Then, we asked ourselves: what are all the unique characters we would interact with in a typical month as we go about our normal life. This gave us our character/persona list.

We then hired a leading voice producer and worked with him to hire voice actors and script writers, and then spent months doing voice recordings in studios in Karachi, Lahore, Quetta and Islamabad.

Once the voices were recorded, then we hired 50 contractors to label data.

The final and the simplest step was the model training. We trained a very small 32M param VITS2 inspired model.

The results are very encouraging.

* **Cost Efficiency at Scale**: In India, every rupee matters. Voice AI must be engineered for efficiency - pre-recorded messages for common utterances, smaller vertical-focused models, and intelligent routing to minimize token usage.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=94216&key=user_uploads/1427127/bb2d0f37-0050-4606-8271-c8664a3d541b)

**The Solution**

Bolna is a **Voice AI Platform** purpose-built for India’s scale, linguistic complexity, and cost sensitivity. We enable enterprises to go live with thousands of concurrent calls in days, not months.

* **Enterprise-grade performance**: Sub-500ms latency, interruption handling, multi-language (10+) and accent (50+) adaptation, fluent in natural multi-language conversations (Hinglish, English + Tamil etc.)
* **India-specific routing**: Bolna automatically picks the optimal model blend for the context, regardless of language, region, or use case.
* **Cost-efficiency engine**: Calls are optimized with pre-recorded inserts, cheaper small models where possible, and routing logic that prioritizes ROI without sacrificing experience.
* **Complete control**: Enterprises define workflows, tone, and intelligence. Bolna handles everything behind the scenes.

Today, Bolna powers **500K+ minutes of calls every month** across BFSI, e-commerce, and recruitment. Customers achieve **higher pickup rates, lower costs, and faster deployments** than with any alternative.

For Indian enterprises, Bolna is not just automation, it is the fastest path to scaling voice operations profitably.

We’ve seen robots on stage: folding laundry, serving popcorn, doing backflips… But before robots get deployed in homes, offices, and shops, they need to become good at **interacting with people**.

launches.body:
Speko is a router for voice models. One API key, and your agent runs on the speech-to-text, LLM and text-to-speech models we measured as best for your language and use case.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=108267&key=user_uploads/451241/2038963f-c769-47a9-8fd9-c59f3966027b)

### I picked voice stacks by trial and error for four years

A voice agent is three models in a row: speech-to-text, then an LLM, then text-to-speech. Three vendors, a dozen credible options each. You run a bake-off, you argue about whose numbers are real, and you ship the combination that felt best that month.

Then next week another model drops. And another. Nobody has time to re-run the bake-off, so the stack you picked under deadline quietly becomes the stack you are stuck with for a year.

That is how most voice agents are running today. Not on the best models. On the models that were best whenever someone last had a free week.

Public leaderboards do not settle it either. They are averages over somebody else's audio, in somebody else's conditions.\
\
[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AjC8WVA96kUBdD09RJMUgFfvxGfxPvL-/](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AjC8WVA96kUBdD09RJMUgFfvxGfxPvL-/view?usp=sharing)

### We measure, then we route

We benchmark the speech models people actually ship on, language by language, and publish everything at [benchmarks.speko.ai](http://benchmarks.speko.ai): word error rate, finalize latency, time to first token, cost per minute. When a vendor ships a new model we test it the same day and the board updates.

Point your agent at Speko and that measurement becomes routing. One API key across every provider we support. Tell us the language and the conditions, and your traffic runs on the stack our numbers say wins. When the numbers change, the routing changes and you rewrite nothing.

If a provider fails when we open the connection, the router drops to the next ranked model on its own.

### Or build the agent with us

You do not need an existing agent to start. A few lines gets a working voice agent live on Speko, and it inherits the same routing from day one.

If you are picking a voice stack right now, start with the numbers at [benchmarks.speko.ai](http://benchmarks.speko.ai), then build on them at [speko.ai](http://speko.ai).

launches.body:
Hey YC, we’re Sahil, Maki, and Tony. We’re building Pluto ([talentpluto.com](https://talentpluto.com/))

Resumes made careers readable. LinkedIn made them searchable. Pluto makes them understood.

<https://youtu.be/gMuOogxpSo4>

**TL;DR** - A professional talks to Pluto for 10 minutes about what they’ve done, what they’re great at, and what they want next. Pluto makes that context discoverable to the right people and AI agents, helping them understand the person more fully. When there’s a real fit, Pluto can also make a warm introduction to a startup.

18K+ professionals have already shared their career context with Pluto. 100+ companies use Pluto to meet people with their full story, including Mercor, David AI, Rho, Warp, and Runlayer.

**Ask:** Talk to Pluto and let it get to know your work. If you’re hiring, send us the role and we’ll introduce you to people with context and confirmed interest.

### **The problem**

A resume and online profile are not enough for the AI era.

They show where someone worked and what title they had. They do not capture what the person actually did, what they are unusually good at, and what they want next.

That context usually lives in conversations. So professionals get reduced to keywords, logos, and titles, while the people and AI agents trying to understand them are left with an incomplete picture. 

Hiring makes this problem obvious. Companies miss great people because the real signal never makes it online. But as AI agents increasingly help people find, evaluate, and connect with one another, every professional will need a richer, more accurate way to be understood.

### **The solution**

Pluto is an AI voice agent that understands a professional’s career and puts that understanding to work.

Professionals talk to Pluto for 10 minutes about their experience, strengths, goals, preferences, and what they want to keep private. Pluto asks follow-up questions, remembers the context missing from their resume, and makes them discoverable to the right people and AI agents.

Companies tell Pluto who they want to meet. Pluto searches its network and the broader market, understands fit on both sides, privately confirms interest, and makes a warm introduction when both sides want to connect. No mass applications. Professionals stay private and in control. Companies meet people who are already understood.

**How It Works**

1. Talk to Pluto for 10 minutes
2. Review what it learned and choose what to share
3. Get found and understood by the right people and AI agents
4. Get introduced to startups when there’s a fit

### **Why We Started This**

The best hiring has always happened through trusted, high-context introductions. We think AI can make that possible for everyone.

Warm introductions are one way Pluto puts that understanding to work today. Long term, Pluto becomes the career context layer for the AI era - the version of a professional’s story that agents can understand, trust, and act on, while the professional stays in control.

### **Our Ask**

If you’re a professional, talk to Pluto and let it get to know your work. 

If you’re a founder, hiring leader, or talent engineer, send us the role you’re hiring for.

[talentpluto.com](http://talentpluto.com)

\- Sahil, Maki, Tony

name: Sona8
long_description:
Sona8 is a voice agent that talks to every employee about how their work gets done. Consulting, transformation and corporate development teams spend a large part of every project on stakeholder interviews and stakeholder alignment, and still only hear from a small share of the people affected.

Each employee gets a link and talks to the agent for about 20 minutes. The agent asks follow-up questions, for example why a step is still done by hand or who else is involved. From the conversations we build process maps and a list of the problems people described, by site and team.

During the implementation, the agent goes back to the employees involved after each initiative and asks whether it was implemented and what changed. The result is a project management office that has talked to every employee. Today consulting firms buy it for the stakeholder interviews at the start of an engagement. Transformation and corporate development teams buy it to run the implementation of a change program.

Over time this becomes the way a company knows how it runs. Sona8 reads the systems the company already uses, connects them to what employees said, and keeps the picture current by asking again. Before a decision, you ask what it would do across sites and teams and get an answer from the whole company. A small team steers a company-wide program that used to need a large one. And AI agents inside the company come here first to learn how the work is done before they change anything.
one_liner: Voice agents that talk to employees enabling transformations

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer: Thilo and I worked on the same consulting project. We did over 70 stakeholder interviews, then had to manage the stakeholders  during implementation, which meant aligning the same people over and over. In the nights we went running a lot in that time. On one of those runs we started asking what if we automated the whole thing. An AI would be strictly better at every step. It asks better questions because it has heard the other interviews, it analyzes with all the context, and it can go back a month later and ask again.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Every big decision in a company is a choice between alternatives. The alternatives you see depend on the context you have. The context that matters most, how the work is done and where the problems are, sits with thousands of employees and never reaches the people who decide.

If we succeed, that context reaches them. Every employee talks to Sona8, and Sona8 plugs into the ERP, the HR system and the ticketing tools. Together that is a live map of how the company runs, and far more than any team can read. The hard part is finding, out of all of it, what matters for one question, and then adding the atomic insights and the judgment. This way, transformation, strategy and consulting teams operate far leaner and faster. Three people steer a program across 20,000 employees.

On top of the map we build a synthetic layer of employees. Before a decision, you run it against that layer and see what it does across sites and teams.

The same map is the enterprise context layer for AI agents. Before an agent changes a process, it reads how that process is done today and by whom. Sona8 is where that map lives.
